root.name: Dutch Defense: Stonewall Variation, Modern Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. g3 c6 5. Bg2 d5 6. O-O Bd6

overview: Black builds the Stonewall pawn wall on f5, e6, d5 and c6, develops the bishop to d6 and aims at the e4 outpost and a kingside attack. White fianchettoes and tries to exploit the weak e5 square and Black's bad light-squared bishop, often with b3, Ba3 or Ne5. The centre is locked and the play is a double-edged fight, with Black attacking on the kingside and White playing on the queenside.

white_ideas.idea: Play Ne5, b3 and Ba3 to trade the dark-squared bishops and exploit weak dark squares.
Occupy e5 with a knight and aim at the bad c8 bishop and a queenside pawn break.

black_ideas.idea: Place a knight on e4, play ...Qe8-h5 and ...g5 for a kingside attack.
Keep the pawn wall and use ...Bd6 and ...Ne4 to secure the e4 outpost.

typical_structures.structure: Stonewall: Black pawns f5/e6/d5/c6 against White d4/c4 and a fianchettoed bishop on g2.

character.notes: Locked centre, kingside attack for Black against White's play on the weak e5 and the bad c8 bishop; double-edged.

soundness.notes: Sound, though Black's bishop is passive.

structure.notes: Pawn wall locks the centre and play moves to the wings.

approach.notes: A set-up Black can play against almost any White move order, hence a system.

level.notes: Clear plans but weak squares need judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Classical Stonewall with ...Be7
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 Nf6 3. g3 e6 4. Bg2 Be7 5. Nf3 O-O 6. O-O d5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black delays ...c6 and keeps the bishop on e7, with similar structures.

character.reason: Unbalanced fight with Black attacking the kingside while White targets e5.

structure.reason: The Stonewall pawns lock the centre.

approach.reason: A set-up Black can play against almost anything.

level.reason: Plans are clear but the bad bishop needs care.

plans.reason: Stonewall chain with an e4 outpost and a hemmed-in bishop.
